    Toolkit & Missing List

    Toolkit used

    • Leaflet — real street map, geolocation, park layers and navigation context.
    • Sites MCP — site registration, source versioning, private deployment.
    • DC Open Data GeoJSON — 230 active DPR properties rendered as polygons.
    • NPS Developer API + NPS.gov — 30 DC-located park units, official descriptions and verified Rock Creek Park visitor facilities.
    • OpenStreetMap tiles — roads, paths, neighborhoods and geographic context.
    • Vanilla HTML/CSS/JS — search, filters, low-power interface and park details.

    Missing / honest limits

    • Functional: the DPR and NPS inventories have no confirmed phone-charging field. Hollow lightning marks indicate recreation centers where staff assistance may exist, not verified outlets.
    • Functional: “Drinking Water” means recorded or officially listed human drinking water only; lakes, ponds and rivers are never included. Counts do not confirm that a fountain is currently operating.
    • NPS facilities: detailed facility markers currently cover official Rock Creek Park locations that NPS explicitly identifies; other NPS units remain marked unverified.
    • Location: browser permission is required, accuracy varies by device, and no location is stored or transmitted by this site.
    • Coverage: DPR polygons and NPS API units use different definitions; some federal sites are points or umbrella units rather than park boundaries.
    • Missing piece: a maintained citywide device-charging dataset or field-verification MCP.

    Sources
